**Conference:** 2nd Model-Informed Drug Development Summit


**Date:** November 18 - 19, 2026


**Location:** Wyndham Boston Beacon Hil, Boston, MA


## Certara is an Expertise Partner of the summit.


Certara is proud to support the 2nd Model-Informed Drug Development Summit, where clinical pharmacology, pharmacometrics, QSP, and regulatory leaders gather around the questions now shaping MIDD in practice: turning model-informed evidence into decisions regulators accept, preparing for ICH M15, and scaling quantitative methods beyond a single program. As the FDA MIDD Pilot Program, Project Optimus, and ICH M15 raise the bar on what sponsors are expected to bring, Certara’s modeling, simulation, and regulatory expertise offers a practical route through the dosing, evidence, and submission questions teams are working through right now.


## Meet Certara at the Summit


[Joshua Apgar, PhD](https://www.certara.com/teams/joshua-apgar-phd/) VP, Head of QSP Software


Dr. Apgar is the VP, Head of QSP Software at Certara, and co-founder of Applied BioMath (acquired by Certara in Dec 2023). Prior to this, Josh was a Principal Scientist in the Systems Biology Group of the Department of Immunology and Inflammation at Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals. His work leveraged physics-based models to: translate in vitro and in vivo data, assess target feasibility, understand drug mechanism of action, and predict human doses. The ultimate goal of this work was to reduce late stage attrition in drug development through a deep and quantitative interrogation of drug pharmacology and disease pathophysiology.


Josh received his PhD from MIT in Biological Engineering where he worked on experiment design for Systems Biology, focusing on the identification of tractable experiments that could allow for the estimation of unknown parameters and reveal complex mechanisms in signal transduction networks. Before that Josh worked at Avaki to develop a highly scalable software platform to support High Performance Computing, and Enterprise Information Integration in the Life Sciences, and Engineering.

## Where to hear Certara insights and expertise


### Speaking session:


Wednesday, Nov 18
12:30–1:00 PM


Model Credibility Is a Patient Safety Issue: How to Build It into Every MIDD Program


**Speaker:** Joshua Apgar, PhD, VP, Head of QSP Software, Certara


Quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP), physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, and pharmacometrics now inform first-in-human doses, drug interaction warnings, and dosing for children and other special populations. Patients take those doses. When a model informs these decisions, a wrong answer can cause harm.


Regulators and internal leaders expect evidence they can inspect, challenge, and reproduce, and ICH M15 now sets out how it will be judged. Most groups can build one credible model. Fewer can do it consistently across every program, with assumptions that hold from discovery through submission and a record reviewers can follow.


AI makes models faster to build, but can widen this credibility gap rather than close it. Drawing on Certara’s work across QSP, PBPK, and pharmacometrics, Joshua Apgar will examine where credibility breaks down in practice and the processes and systems that prevent failures without slowing progress.


**Attendees will leave with five practical questions to test their MIDD processes before their next regulatory interaction.**


Key Takeaways


- Why credibility matters: How the success of QSP, PBPK, and pharmacometrics has raised the stakes for patient safety and what ICH M15 means for modeling groups.
- Where credibility breaks down: Vague questions, criteria set after results, drift between models, and work that cannot be reproduced.
- How to make credible work the norm: The processes and systems that support model credibility across every program, including the safe use of AI.


### Scientific poster:


Poster session, Day 1, 3:30 pm


Certara IQ: Regulatory-Grade QSP on Every Program, from Plan to Report


**Authors:** Joshua F. Apgar¹, David Flowers¹, David Hagan¹, Andrew Matteson¹, Piet H. van der Graaf¹˒² **Affiliations:** ¹ Certara. ² Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research, Leiden University.


ICH M15, FDA’s 2026 draft guidance on QSP-based MABEL dosing and the FDA Fit-for-Purpose program set one life cycle for QSP evidence: plan, build, evaluate, report and update. Certara IQ builds that life cycle into a single cloud platform. Workflow templates structure the question, context of use and model risk. Models are checked for units and syntax on every edit. Analyses run on built-in high-performance computing. Version history, provenance and an audit trail come standard. An AI assistant writes and debugs model code, and a scientist clears every change. A worked first-in-human example takes a T-cell engager from in vitro data to a human starting dose. The result is faster, consistent, auditable QSP on every program.
